parameters.content:
## Create narrated faceless Shorts from any topic with the Meta Muse API

**Who it's for:** faceless YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Reels channels: history, science, "did you know" and explainer pages.

It runs on **your own Muse account** through the [useapi.net Muse API](https://useapi.net/docs/api-muse-v1?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-faceless-shorts), **a third-party API, not affiliated with Meta**.

**How it works**
1. The form takes a topic, 1 to 3 scenes, a look and a voice mode.
2. A Muse chat writes the script: one spoken line and one shot per scene. Edit it, or ask for a new one.
3. Muse makes one 10-second vertical clip per scene, side by side. It narrates each line, or (locked voice) lays its own text-to-speech file on each clip, so every scene has the same voice.
4. **Your scenes** plays them. Redo any scene with a new line or shot.
5. A Muse chat joins the clips into one MP4. The result page plays it, shows the % of the week the run used, and can save it to Google Drive.

**Errors:** busy and "nothing made" answers are retried. A job that may already have used the allowance is never sent again: it stops with its job id.

**Set up**
1. Get a [useapi.net API token](https://useapi.net/docs/start-here/setup-useapi?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-faceless-shorts) and add your Muse account with [Setup Muse](https://useapi.net/docs/start-here/setup-muse?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-faceless-shorts).
2. Create a **Header Auth** credential: Name `Authorization`, Value `Bearer <your token>`. Select it on every HTTP Request node.
3. Create a **Basic Auth** credential (any username and password) and select it on **Make a faceless Short**.
4. Publish (activate) the workflow and open the form URL.

**Requirements:** a useapi.net subscription and a Muse account created in the US or Canada (as of October 2026). The free Muse plan works: in our tests a 10-second clip used about 2-3% of the week, and the chats 0%.

**Customize:** the prompts, defaults and Drive folder are at the top of **Read the form**. Code and screenshots: [GitHub](https://github.com/useapi/muse-api).

### 1. Form + script
**Read account** reads the live weekly allowance and pins the run to one Muse account (the join needs every clip on it). A Muse chat writes the script as JSON; code fences are stripped and a reply that can't be read gets one new chat. **Your script** lets you edit each line and shot.

### 2. Muse chats
The script, the voice files and the join all go through these nodes: **POST /chats**, then **GET /chats/{chatId}** every 8 s until the answer is complete. Muse's permission requests are denied: none of these chats needs the web or a public link. Each chat also shows in your muse.ai app.

### 3. Locked voice (optional)
One chat reads every line with Muse text to speech in the voice you chose, and saves the MP3s in your workspace under this run's names. They are matched to the scenes by name. A missing file gets one more chat.

### 4. Clips + pick or redo
**POST /jobs/video** per scene, side by side, polled every 15 s. The ratio and the spoken line go in the prompt. With a voice file as `audio_1`, Muse lays it onto its clip and the job returns that file first (`origin: made`). `429` and `503` (nothing made) are sent again after 30 s; nothing else is. Locked-voice clips are copied at once with a free upload, so a later clip can't replace them. **Your scenes** lets you redo any scene.

### 5. Join + result + Google Drive
A chat joins the clips with ffmpeg into one MP4 and attaches it (no public links). Optional Drive upload. **Read account (after)** gives the real cost: the % used before and after. Files stay in your Muse workspace until you delete them.

### 6. Stops
A page says what to fix: token (`401`), account (`404`, `596`), allowance (`412`, with the reset time). `500`, `502`, `504` or no answer may already have used the allowance: never resent, the page shows the job id to check.

### 7. Media file (players and downloads)
The players and download links call this webhook. It fetches the file with your credential, so the token never reaches the browser. Each link carries a ticket signed with a random secret (made once by **New secret**) that expires after 24 h; the webhook never takes an asset id or a URL, and answers 404 to anything else.
